properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL — 2026-08-11, from Anthony's observation that the governance work came from a real demand signal ("it was all taken from feedback from the storyflow project... I told reflow2 to consider it and do it"). Nothing here is intent.

WHAT WAS MEASURED, and it is the reason the question exists. reflow2's own governance requirements DID come from a demand signal: `/home/ajs7/project/dev_storyflow/reflow2_feedback.md`, the GOVERNANCE-AS-DESIGN entry by api-boss, 2026-08-08. Six Requirements carry AUTHORED_BY to `who:storyflow-api-boss`, so the authorship survived. But:

  · searched every node in the design for the string `reflow2_feedback` → 12 hits, NONE of them any of the six governance requirements
  · the document is not registered as an Artifact
  · so the origin of this work exists only in Anthony's head, and he had to tell an agent where to look

⭐ THE SELF-INDICTMENT: `req:no-idea-goes-quiet` is ACCEPTED and reads "an idea in the graph stays connected to whether it was built and to where it was written — THE USER NEVER HUNTS FOR THE SOURCE DOCUMENT AGAIN." reflow2's own governance capture violates an accepted reflow2 requirement, and no detector could see it.

⭐ AND IT COST SOMETHING MEASURABLE, twice. The feedback entry ranked THREE asks. Only #1 reached the graph:
  #1  model VERIFIES onto DesignRule so enforced+no-check is detectable   → BUILT (unverified_enforced_rule)
  #2  a Role/Seat node distinct from Contributor — duties attach to the
      SEAT, not the human                                                 → ABSENT, no such node type
  #3  an `obligation` category on DesignRule: "MUST do X AT MOMENT Y"     → ABSENT; categories in use
                                                                             are convention/methodology/None
#3 carried the sharpest sentence in the entry — "our doc map recorded WHO reads a file and WHAT it holds, and never WHEN — the missing axis was TIME, and no rule was being broken because no rule named a moment." That finding is nowhere in this design. The entry did say #1 was "the whole idea's leverage and the rest is optional", so building #1 first was RIGHT — but #2 and #3 were not DEFERRED, they evaporated, which is a different thing and the one nobody can see.

IDEAS, unranked:
(a) A gap for a Requirement with no incoming DOCUMENTS/Fragment/origin edge — "what asked for this?"
(b) No new detector; instead make the capture skills register the source document as an Artifact by default, so the edge exists by construction rather than by discipline.
(c) Do nothing structural, and treat the origin as prose in the requirement's own statement.

COUNTER-ARGUMENT TO (a), and it is the same trap that made `rule:a-design-is-named-by-an-id-not-a-path` advisory: at genesis NOBODY has a source document — intent arrives by someone talking. A detector demanding an origin edge would fire against the entire design on day one and the only way to green it would be to fabricate origins. That argues (b) is the honest shape and (a) is only safe if it fires on requirements whose provenance says they came from a DOCUMENT.

NOTE ON WHY THE DAU FRAME FITS: of the nine DAU requirement characteristics Anthony cited, TRACEABLE is defined as connecting "directly back to top-level strategic guidance and forward to system design specs." reflow2 checks FORWARD (the golden thread; unmotivated_capability fired on exactly this) and has no check at all for BACKWARD. COMPLETE failed too — 2 of 3 ranked asks are absent in any form.
properties.name: OPEN — should a Requirement with no recorded ORIGIN be a gap? The golden thread checks forward and nothing checks backward
properties.rationale: The demand signal existed and became requirements — the process was run. What broke was traceability backward to the source and completeness across the source's three asks. Both are invisible to every detector reflow2 has, and an accepted requirement already says they should not be.
